12. Anemia is very common in patients with CKD. Why does it 
occur, and how is it treated?
CKD patients are not able to synthesize adequate amounts 
of endogenous erythropoietin, a hormone that is made
by renal tubular cells, which leads to decreased red cell 
production in the bone marrow and low hemoglobin (Hgb) 
levels. Unlike PD patients, HD patients also incur increased
blood loss from dialysis procedures. Th e discovery of 
recombinant human erythropoietin (rHuEPO) was a major 
breakthrough and has signiﬁ cantly improved the quality of 
life in CKD patients. Treatment with rHuEPO and iron is 
common practice today.
